Subject: Private cluster: surge in 503s and p95 latency — urgent

Karthik,

We started seeing a significant degradation this morning after the 03:00 cluster maintenance window. Transactional requests to the payment-embedding route are returning ~6% 503s and p95 latency has jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s. This is impacting checkout flows for 25% of our users. Our ops team pulled logs and attached the snippets — there are repeated kernel timeouts and 'KV cache miss / mismatch' messages.

We are on Redwood Private (VPC) v1.12 with the quantized 8-bit model bundle you recommended. This is a production-facing payment path, and leadership is asking for an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA for a fix. We need either a config rollback or an emergency patch and an SLA credit conversation if this cannot be restored quickly.

Attaching: error_log_snippets.txt, p95_traces_20261002.zip

Please escalate.

— Alex

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private cluster: surge in 503s and p95 latency — urgent

Karthik / Monica / Evelyn,

Initial triage notes from infra: we reproduced a p95 regression on a staging gate with the same quantization bundle + newer kernel set. Two immediate observations:
1) The newer kernel path introduces a suboptimal attention kernel for long-context batches — manifests as CPU-side stalls under our current async batching window.
2) The KV cache code path in v1.12 has a race condition when cache evictions collide with quantized weight swaps — that can throw transient "KV cache mismatch" and escalate to request-level 503s.

Short-term mitigations we can apply right now (recommended order):
A) Force traffic to the non-quantized model variant we keep for fallback (zero code change, just routing update) — estimated customer-visible reduction in 503s within 3–7 minutes.
B) Roll back the kernel set on the affected inferencer nodes to the previous release (requires rolling restart of 6 nodes, ~25 minutes to complete).
C) If they accept a brief maintenance window, we can perform a controlled cache flush + sequential restart to remove racing state (~35 minutes).

I can execute A immediately with permission. Longer-term, we need a patch for the KV eviction race and a better pre-release test that includes quantized+kernel combos. I'll open INF-4921 with details and a PR plan.

— Vivek
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@enterprisecx.com>, Sara Lim <sara.lim@enterprisecx.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Exec note + immediate mitigation for EnterpriseCX — request for approval

Alex / Sara — quick update and next steps, in plain terms for execs:

What happened: after a routine maintenance window this morning, EnterpriseCX's VPC deployment started experiencing increased 503s and higher p95 latency on the payment-embedding route. We identified a compatibility problem between our most recent kernel optimizations and the quantized model variant. This can cause transient KV cache mismatches that surface as 503s.

Immediate mitigation (we recommend and seek approval to apply now):
- Route traffic to EnterpriseCX's non-quantized model variant (automatic fallback) — expected to reduce 503s to <0.5% and restore p95 to pre-incident numbers within ~10 minutes.
- Schedule a 30–40 minute maintenance window to perform a controlled cache flush and rolling restarts (customer-visible ~35 minutes downtime on affected routes).

Executive asks:
1) We recommend offering an SLA credit for the downtime window (we estimate exposure for 25% of checkouts). Monica — please propose a credit figure under our policy and confirm who signs the exception.
2) We will need to escalate a high-priority engineering patch for the KV eviction race (INF-4921). Vivek will lead and provide ETA for the patch within 48 hours.
3) If EnterpriseCX requests a white-glove rollback or dedicated engineering hours, confirm available slots this week.

Alex — can you confirm: (A) approve the immediate routing change, and (B) whether you prefer we proceed with the maintenance window tonight at 22:00 PT or ASAP this afternoon?

I will call you in 5 to talk through and pull in legal/finance if a formal credit note is required.

— Karthik
